title: KCNA Master Question Set 5 — Application Delivery, GitOps & CI/CD
description: Comprehensive KCNA practice exam set #5 containing 300 real-world practice questions aligned with Linux Foundation exam blueprint.

questions.question: Which Kubernetes control plane component acts as the primary frontend for the cluster REST API and handles authentication/authorization?
options: kube-scheduler
kube-apiserver
etcd
kube-controller-manager
questions.explanation: The kube-apiserver is the only component that directly communicates with etcd and validates all API calls.

questions.question: What is the role of etcd in a Kubernetes cluster?
options: Executes container images on worker nodes
Consistent and highly available key-value store for all cluster data
Schedules Pods onto appropriate worker nodes
Manages cloud provider load balancers
questions.explanation: etcd is a distributed key-value store used as Kubernetes backing store for all cluster state.

questions.question: How are Kubernetes Network Policies applied to Pods to govern ingress and egress communication?
options: Using iptables commands on individual containers
Using label selectors to identify target Pods
By modifying host /etc/hosts files
Through DNS TXT record entries
questions.explanation: NetworkPolicies use label selectors to select pods and define rules for allowed traffic.

questions.question: What does a StorageClass provide in Kubernetes storage architecture?
options: Direct root SSH access to storage servers
A way for administrators to describe the classes of storage and enable dynamic provisioning
Automatic backup of all database tables
Network encryption for pod-to-pod traffic
questions.explanation: StorageClass allows dynamic provisioning of PersistentVolumes based on parameters defined by the cluster administrator.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the Open Container Initiative (OCI)?
options: To build cloud hardware servers
To define open industry standards for container image formats and runtime specifications
To replace Linux kernels with proprietary OS
To manage DNS routing across public cloud providers
questions.explanation: The OCI establishes industry specifications around container formats and runtimes (such as runc).

questions.question: In Cloud Native Observability and SRE terminology, what is a Service Level Indicator (SLI)?
options: A legally binding financial contract with customers
A carefully measured quantitative metric of service performance (e.g., latency, error rate)
The target uptime goal set by product managers
An automated restart policy for failing pods
questions.explanation: An SLI is a direct measurement of behavior, whereas an SLO is the target objective for that indicator.

questions.question: Which principle is core to GitOps methodology in cloud-native application delivery?
options: Manual FTP upload of binary files to production servers
Git repository as the single source of truth for declarative infrastructure and application state
Hardcoding API secrets inside Docker images
Disabling continuous integration testing for speed
questions.explanation: GitOps uses Git repositories as the declarative source of truth and continuously reconciles the cluster state.

questions.question: What is the key difference between a Kubernetes Role and a ClusterRole?
options: A Role is namespace-scoped, whereas a ClusterRole is cluster-scoped
A ClusterRole can only be used by Linux kernel drivers
A Role cannot grant read permissions
There is no difference; they are synonymous
questions.explanation: Roles grant permissions within a specific namespace, while ClusterRoles grant cluster-wide permissions.

questions.question: Which Prometheus metric type represents a cumulative metric that only increases or resets to zero on restart?
options: Gauge
Counter
Histogram
Summary
questions.explanation: A Counter is a cumulative metric that represents a single monotonically increasing counter.

questions.question: When do Init Containers run in a Kubernetes Pod lifecycle?
options: Concurrently with application containers throughout the entire lifetime
Sequentially before app containers start, running to completion
Only after the Pod is deleted during termination
Whenever CPU utilization exceeds 90%
questions.explanation: Init containers run before app containers and each init container must run to completion before the next starts.

questions.question: [KCNA Scenario #11] In the context of Cloud Native Application Delivery, which statement best describes the role of Container Image Security?
options: It provides declarative orchestration and automated lifecycle management for cloud-native workloads.
It replaces the Linux filesystem with a proprietary monolithic storage layer.
It requires all developer workstations to run bare-metal hypervisors.
It disables network encryption to maximize network throughput.
questions.explanation: Within Cloud Native Application Delivery, Container Image Security focuses on declarative automation, scalability, and standards-compliant cloud-native engineering.

questions.question: [KCNA Scenario #12] Which CNCF specification or standard is most relevant when working with Application Lifecycle in Cloud Native Application Delivery?
options: Open Container Initiative (OCI) and Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) best practices
Proprietary mainframe assembly language commands
Static hardcoded IP routing without service discovery
Manual SSH shell scripting on production worker nodes
questions.explanation: CNCF and OCI specifications provide vendor-neutral standards that ensure interoperability across modern cloud-native architectures.

questions.question: [KCNA Practice #13] When deploying cloud-native applications involving GitOps & ArgoCD/Flux, what is the primary benefit of declarative YAML configuration?
options: It guarantees zero bugs in user application logic
It allows version-controlled, repeatable desired-state reconciliation by control plane controllers
It prevents Kubernetes from scheduling containers on more than one node
It eliminates the need for persistent volumes or storage classes
questions.explanation: Declarative YAML configurations enable GitOps, automation, and continuous desired-state reconciliation by Kubernetes controllers.

questions.question: [KCNA Practice #14] An engineer needs to debug a failure related to CI/CD Pipelines. Which Kubernetes or Cloud Native approach is recommended?
options: Reboot all physical hardware routers in the datacenter
Examine structured logs, Prometheus metrics, and Kubernetes events/descriptions
Disable Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) globally across all clusters
Delete etcd snapshots without backup
questions.explanation: Cloud-native observability relies on logs, metrics (e.g. Prometheus), tracing, and Kubernetes API events to troubleshoot issues safely.

questions.question: [KCNA Practice #15] How does Helm Charts & Package Management enhance security and reliability in a Cloud Native Application Delivery deployment?
options: By enforcing least-privilege access, immutable container images, and automated health probes
By granting root privileges to all container processes by default
By bypassing Container Network Interface (CNI) plugins
By storing API tokens in plain text in ConfigMaps
questions.explanation: Cloud-native security best practices include least privilege (RBAC), immutable artifacts, network segmentation, and automated liveness/readiness probes.
